text: Of David, when he feigned madness before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he left.
I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise will always be on my lips.
My soul boasts in the LORD; let the humble hear and rejoice.
Magnify the LORD with me; let us exalt his name together.
I sought the LORD, and he answered me; he delivered me from all my fears.
Those who look to him are radiant; their faces will never be ashamed.

versions.text: Those who look to him are radiant; their faces are never covered with shame.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb חָפֵר means to be ashamed or disgraced; "covered with shame" adds an image not present in the text and is heavier for oral reading than the simpler wording.

text: This poor man called, and the LORD heard; he saved him out of all his troubles.
The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and he rescues them.
Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the one who takes refuge in him.
Fear the LORD, you his holy ones, for those who fear him lack nothing.
Young lions grow poor and hungry, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.

versions.text: Young lions go weak with hunger, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct verbs, רָשׁוּ (become poor/destitute) and וְרָעֵבוּ (go hungry). "Go weak with hunger" collapses them into one idea and loses the deliberate contrast with "lack no good thing."

text: Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
Who is the one who delights in life and loves many days, to see good?

versions.text: Who is the one who delights in life and longs for days of good?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has "loves days" plus the purpose clause "to see good" (לִרְאוֹת טוֹב). The current wording folds the purpose clause into a noun phrase, losing the movement of the line that leads into the instruction of the following verses.

text: Guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their cry.
The face of the LORD is set against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth.
They cried out, and the LORD heard; he delivered them from all their troubles.
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; he saves those crushed in spirit.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
He watches over all his bones; not one of them is broken.
Evil will put the wicked to death, and those who hate the righteous will bear their guilt.
The LORD redeems the life of his servants; no one who takes refuge in him will bear guilt.

versions.text: The LORD redeems the life of his servants; no one who takes refuge in him will be condemned.
versions.explanation: The same verb (אָשַׁם) is used in verse 22 and verse 23, forming a deliberate link between the fate of the wicked and the safety of the faithful. Rendering it "bear guilt" here, as in verse 22, preserves that echo; "condemned" also imports a slightly stronger judicial sense than the Hebrew.
